newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Tajikistan hands maverick fighter ultimatum.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan hands maverick fighter ultimatum.

text.p: Tajikistan said on Wednesday it would use all military means to wipe out an armed band led by maverick fighter and hostage-taker Rizvon Sadirov if they failed to surrender by Wednesday evening.
"The government side has given Sadirov an ultimatum -- his group must lay down arms by the evening," presidential spokesman Zafar Saidov told Reuters by telephone from the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
General Gafor Mirzoyev, commander of the presidential guard, also told Reuters: "If Sadirov does not surrender, we will use tough force measures to liquidate the group."
Sadirov once fought for Tajikistan's Islamic opposition against the secular government of the remote, mountainous former Soviet republic but his loyalties are now unclear.

Last December, the group seized a group of foreigners working in Tajikistan. In February, Sadirov's brother Bakhrom held 14 international aid workers, foreign military observers and Russian journalists for nearly two weeks.
The brothers demanded free passage for their men to return to the country from bases in neighbouring Afghanistan. The government bowed to all conditions.

The wild-card brothers have proved important politically in the chronically unstable country and the government joined forces to hunt them down with units of the country's Islamic opposition, its former foes in a bitter four-year civil war.
Last December, the secular government and the opposition agreed a ceasefire which seems to be holding and are hammering out details of a new power-sharing arrangement.
Bakhrom Sadirov and around 20 of his men were arrested and brought to Dushanbe at the weekend.
But Mirzoyev said that Rizvon and about 45 of his fighters were still hiding in the treacherous approaches to the Pamir mountains about 80 km (50 miles) east of Dushanbe.
Attempts by government and opposition forces at the weekend to flush Rizvon out of the republic's mountain fastnesses failed.
But Mirzoyev said "One of those captured together with Bakhrom on Saturday has been released and reached Rizvon's base to tell him that further resistance was senseless and he must surrender."
